## YAML helpers

block style, two-space indents, and lines up to 120 characters. Use it
when you read or write workflow YAML yourself, so your output is
formatted the same way as gheasy’s.

## Step builder

[`WorkflowNode`](https://vedicreader.github.io/gheasy/workflow.html#workflownode)
is the base class that gives every builder `job()` and `build()`.
[`StepBuilder`](https://vedicreader.github.io/gheasy/workflow.html#stepbuilder)
describes one step. You rarely create one yourself:
`JobBuilder.step(name)` makes it and adds it to the job.

``` python
def StepBuilder(
    name:str, job
):
```

*Fluent builder for a single workflow step.*

### Core step fields

A step does one of two things. `run` gives it a shell command, and
`uses` names an action to run instead, with `with_` supplying the
action’s inputs. The other methods set optional fields. `env` adds
environment variables, `id` names the step so later steps can read its
outputs, `if_` runs it only when a condition holds, `continue_on_error`
lets the job carry on when the step fails, `timeout_minutes` limits how
long it may take, and `working_directory` sets the folder a `run`
command starts in. `if_` and `with_` end in an underscore because `if`
and `with` are Python keywords.

------------------------------------------------------------------------

<a
href="https://github.com/vedicreader/gheasy/blob/main/gheasy/workflow.py#L107"
target="_blank" style="float:right; font-size:smaller">source</a>

### Action shortcuts

These fill in `uses` and `with` for actions most workflows need.
`checkout` fetches the repository, and `fetch_depth=0` fetches its whole
history rather than only the latest commit. `setup_python` and
`setup_node` install a language version and cache its packages. `cache`
saves a folder at the end of a run and restores it at the start of the
next one whose `key` matches. `upload_artifact` and `download_artifact`
pass files from one job to another, and
[`docker_build_push`](https://vedicreader.github.io/gheasy/workflow.html#docker_build_push)
builds a Docker image and, with `push=True`, pushes it.

href="https://github.com/vedicreader/gheasy/blob/main/gheasy/workflow.py#L165"
target="_blank" style="float:right; font-size:smaller">source</a>

## Strategy / matrix builder

A matrix runs the same job several times with different values, for
example once per Python version or operating system.
[`JobBuilder.strategy()`](https://vedicreader.github.io/gheasy/workflow.html#jobbuilder.strategy)
returns a
[`StrategyBuilder`](https://vedicreader.github.io/gheasy/workflow.html#strategybuilder).
`matrix` sets the lists of values to combine, `include` adds one extra
combination and `exclude` removes one, `fail_fast(False)` keeps the
other combinations running when one fails, and `max_parallel` limits how
many run at the same time. Steps read the current values as expressions
such as `${{ matrix.python-version }}`. `end_strategy()` returns to the
job. The job writes a `strategy` block when `matrix`, `include`,
`exclude` or `fail_fast` was called. `max_parallel` alone produces no
block. `include` and `exclude` turn underscores in keyword names into
hyphens like `matrix` does, so `python_version` in either one matches
the `python-version` key of the matrix. Values are left as written.

------------------------------------------------------------------------

<a
href="https://github.com/vedicreader/gheasy/blob/main/gheasy/workflow.py#L195"
target="_blank" style="float:right; font-size:smaller">source</a>

### StrategyBuilder

``` python
def StrategyBuilder(
    _job:Any, _matrix:dict[str, list[typing.Any]]=<factory>, _fail_fast:bool | None=None,
    _max_parallel:int | None=None, _include:list[dict]=<factory>, _exclude:list[dict]=<factory>
)->None:
```

*Builder for a job’s `strategy` block, which runs the job once per
combination of matrix values.*

## Job builder

[`JobBuilder`](https://vedicreader.github.io/gheasy/workflow.html#jobbuilder)
describes one job. `WorkflowBuilder.job(job_id)` creates it. The id is
the key the job appears under in the YAML, and the name other jobs use
to wait for it in `needs`.

------------------------------------------------------------------------

<a
href="https://github.com/vedicreader/gheasy/blob/main/gheasy/workflow.py#L242"
target="_blank" style="float:right; font-size:smaller">source</a>

### JobBuilder

``` python
def JobBuilder(
    job_id:str, workflow
):
```

*Fluent builder for a single workflow job.*

### Job-level fields

Every job needs `runs_on`, the label of the runner such as
`ubuntu-latest`. `needs` makes the job wait until other jobs have
succeeded. `if_`, `timeout_minutes` and `continue_on_error` work as they
do for steps. `env` sets variables for all the job’s steps, and
`permissions` sets what the job’s `GITHUB_TOKEN` may do. `outputs`
publishes values that later jobs read as `needs.<job>.outputs.<name>`.
`concurrency` keeps two runs of the job in the same group from
overlapping, and cancels the older run unless
`cancel_in_progress=False`. `services` starts helper containers beside
the job, such as a database for integration tests, and `container` runs
the job’s steps inside a Docker image. `environment` ties the job to a
GitHub environment, which can hold its own secrets and can require
someone’s approval before the job runs.

------------------------------------------------------------------------

<a
href="https://github.com/vedicreader/gheasy/blob/main/gheasy/workflow.py#L318"
target="_blank" style="float:right; font-size:smaller">source</a>

### Strategy and steps

`strategy()` starts a matrix, and `step(name)` adds an empty step for
you to fill in. The other methods each add one ready-made step and
return it. `checkout`, `setup_python` and `setup_node` wrap the step
shortcuts above. `install` and `run_tests` add a pip install command and
a test command. `setup_uv`, `uv_install` and `uv_run` do the same with
uv. `setup_uv` installs uv itself, `uv_install` runs `uv sync --frozen`
by default, and `uv_run(cmd)` runs `uv run cmd`. `uv_run` names the step
after the first word of `cmd`, capitalized.

------------------------------------------------------------------------

<a
href="https://github.com/vedicreader/gheasy/blob/main/gheasy/workflow.py#L375"
target="_blank" style="float:right; font-size:smaller">source</a>

## Trigger builder

Triggers are the events that start a workflow, and they go under `on:`
in the YAML. Every
[`WorkflowBuilder`](https://vedicreader.github.io/gheasy/workflow.html#workflowbuilder)
has a
[`TriggerBuilder`](https://vedicreader.github.io/gheasy/workflow.html#triggerbuilder)
as its `on` attribute. Each trigger method adds one event and returns
the trigger builder, so events chain:
`wfb.on.push(branches=['main']).pull_request()`. Writing `.on` again
partway along a chain is allowed and changes nothing. `done` returns to
the workflow when the chain carries on with workflow methods.

------------------------------------------------------------------------

<a
href="https://github.com/vedicreader/gheasy/blob/main/gheasy/workflow.py#L394"
target="_blank" style="float:right; font-size:smaller">source</a>

### TriggerBuilder

``` python
def TriggerBuilder(
    workflow
):
```

*Builder for the events that start a workflow, its `on:` block.*

### Push and pull request triggers

`push` and `pull_request` can be limited to some branches, tags or
paths, so that, for example, a change to the docs does not run the test
suite. `pull_request_target` runs with the target repository’s
permissions and secrets, even for pull requests from forks, so never use
it to run code from the pull request.

------------------------------------------------------------------------

<a
href="https://github.com/vedicreader/gheasy/blob/main/gheasy/workflow.py#L425"
target="_blank" style="float:right; font-size:smaller">source</a>

### Schedule and dispatch triggers

`schedule` runs the workflow on a cron timetable, in UTC, and can be
called more than once to add several times. `workflow_dispatch` adds a
Run workflow button to the repository’s Actions tab, with optional
inputs to fill in. `workflow_call` lets other workflows call this one as
a reusable workflow.

issue or an issue comment, a package published to GitHub’s registry, a
branch or tag being created or deleted, a fork, or a GitHub Pages build.

`['published']` for releases.

### Navigation and rendering

With no triggers, the `on` block is an empty mapping. With exactly one
trigger that has no options, such as `create()`, the block is that event
name alone. With any other combination, the block is a mapping from each
event to its options, and an event without options has no value. Calling
a trigger method again replaces the earlier options for that event,
except `schedule`, which adds a time.

### Configuration

These set fields that apply to the whole workflow. `run_name` sets the
title each run shows in the Actions tab, and accepts expressions.
`permissions` sets what the workflow’s `GITHUB_TOKEN` may do, with the
value `read`, `write` or `none` for each scope. `env` sets variables for
every job, and `concurrency` stops two runs in the same group from
overlapping, cancelling the older one by default.
`job(job_id, needs=None)` adds a job and returns it, and `build()`
returns the finished
[`WorkflowDoc`](https://vedicreader.github.io/gheasy/workflow.html#workflowdoc).

### Job presets

A preset adds a complete job in one call and returns the workflow
builder. Presets chain one after another. `uv_test_job` checks out the
code, installs uv, runs `uv sync --frozen`, and runs `uv run pytest` or
the `test_cmd` you give. With `python_versions`, it adds a matrix over
those versions. `uv_lint_job` does the same setup and runs ruff.
`uv_pypi_job` builds with `uv build` and uploads to PyPI through trusted
publishing, which needs no API token but does need the project set up as
a trusted publisher on PyPI. It runs only when a release starts the
workflow, and waits for `test` unless you change `needs`. `docker_job`
logs in to GHCR and pushes the image tagged `latest`, also after `test`.
`node_job`, `rust_job` and `go_job` add a build-and-test job for those
languages.

Each preset uses a fixed job id: `test`, `lint`, `publish`, `docker`,
`frontend`, `rust` and `go`. Calling one preset twice writes one job
under that id, and the later call replaces the earlier one in the YAML.

``` python
wfb = Workflow('ci')
wfb.on.push(branches=['main'])
doc = wfb.uv_test_job().uv_lint_job().uv_pypi_job().build()
```

<a
href="https://github.com/vedicreader/gheasy/blob/main/gheasy/workflow.py#L633"
target="_blank" style="float:right; font-size:smaller">source</a>

### GitHub API

These call GitHub directly and need a token, passed as `token` or set as
`GITHUB_TOKEN`. All three take the workflow’s file name to be its `name`
plus `.yml`. Give the workflow a name that works as a file name. Without
a token, each raises `ValueError`. `upload` commits the YAML to
`.github/workflows/<name>.yml` on `branch`, creating or replacing the
file. Its default commit message is
`ci: add/update <name>.yml workflow [ghaflow]`, and `commit_message`
replaces it. `dispatch` starts a run on `ref`, which only works for a
workflow with a `workflow_dispatch` trigger that is already committed to
the repository. `list_runs` returns the most recent `per_page` runs, 10
by default.

------------------------------------------------------------------------

<a
href="https://github.com/vedicreader/gheasy/blob/main/gheasy/workflow.py#L701"
target="_blank" style="float:right; font-size:smaller">source</a>

## Entry point

`Workflow(name)` is where every chain starts. It returns a new
[`WorkflowBuilder`](https://vedicreader.github.io/gheasy/workflow.html#workflowbuilder),
and `name` becomes the workflow’s title in the Actions tab.

------------------------------------------------------------------------

<a
href="https://github.com/vedicreader/gheasy/blob/main/gheasy/workflow.py#L722"
target="_blank" style="float:right; font-size:smaller">source</a>

### Workflow

``` python
def Workflow(
    name:str
)->__main__.WorkflowBuilder:
```

*Start building a workflow called `name`.*

## Recipes

A recipe returns a finished
[`WorkflowDoc`](https://vedicreader.github.io/gheasy/workflow.html#workflowdoc)
for a common whole workflow, ready to save.
[`docker_build_push`](https://vedicreader.github.io/gheasy/workflow.html#docker_build_push)
builds a Docker image on every push to the given branches and pushes it
to GHCR, with tags chosen by `docker/metadata-action`. With its default
settings that action names the tag after the branch that was pushed. Use
it for images you deploy from several branches. The `docker_job` preset,
with its single `latest` tag, suits one image from one branch. This
recipe has the same name as the
[`StepBuilder.docker_build_push`](https://vedicreader.github.io/gheasy/workflow.html#stepbuilder.docker_build_push)
step shortcut, and it is a separate function.
[`pages_deploy`](https://vedicreader.github.io/gheasy/workflow.html#pages_deploy)
builds a static site with npm and publishes the output folder to GitHub
Pages. It runs on pushes to
[`main`](https://vedicreader.github.io/gheasy/core.html#main) and on
manual dispatch.
[`uv_ci`](https://vedicreader.github.io/gheasy/workflow.html#uv_ci) is
the standard Python CI. It runs a `lint` job with ruff, then a `test`
job, both using uv, on pushes and pull requests to the given branches.
With `lint_cmd=None` it leaves out the `lint` job. `test_cmd=None` is
not supported and writes the command `uv run None`.

------------------------------------------------------------------------

<a
href="https://github.com/vedicreader/gheasy/blob/main/gheasy/workflow.py#L750"
target="_blank" style="float:right; font-size:smaller">source</a>

## Tests

### Test helpers

``` python
from fastcore.test import test_eq
from ruamel.yaml import YAML as _YAML
def parse_yaml(text): return _YAML().load(text)
def yaml_of(doc): return parse_yaml(doc.to_yaml())
```

``` python
# end_step() returns JobBuilder
wfb = Workflow('ci')
jb = wfb.on.push().job('test').runs_on('ubuntu-latest')
sb = jb.step('Run').run('pytest')
result = sb.end_step()
assert hasattr(result, '_steps'), f"expected JobBuilder, got {type(result)}"

# end_job() on StepBuilder returns WorkflowBuilder
result2 = sb.end_job()
assert hasattr(result2, 'build') and hasattr(result2, '_jobs'), f"expected WorkflowBuilder, got {type(result2)}"
print('end_step/end_job OK')
```

    end_step/end_job OK

### Step builder

#### Tests

``` python
# TestSteps
doc = (Workflow('ci').on.push()
    .job('test').runs_on('ubuntu-latest')
    .step('Checkout').uses('actions/checkout@v4')
    .build())
y = yaml_of(doc)
steps = y['jobs']['test']['steps']
test_eq(steps[0]['name'], 'Checkout')
test_eq(steps[0]['uses'], 'actions/checkout@v4')

doc = (Workflow('ci').on.push()
    .job('test').runs_on('ubuntu-latest')
    .step('Install').run("pip install -e '.[dev]'")
    .build())
y = yaml_of(doc)
test_eq(y['jobs']['test']['steps'][0]['run'], "pip install -e '.[dev]'")

doc = (Workflow('ci').on.push()
    .job('test').runs_on('ubuntu-latest')
    .step('Setup Python').uses('actions/setup-python@v5').with_(python_version='3.12', cache='pip')
    .build())
y = yaml_of(doc)
w = y['jobs']['test']['steps'][0]['with']
test_eq(w['python-version'], '3.12')
test_eq(w['cache'], 'pip')

doc = (Workflow('ci').on.push()
    .job('test').runs_on('ubuntu-latest')
    .step('Get version').run('echo VERSION=$(cat VERSION)').id('get_version')
    .build())
y = yaml_of(doc)
test_eq(y['jobs']['test']['steps'][0]['id'], 'get_version')

doc = (Workflow('ci').on.push()
    .job('test').runs_on('ubuntu-latest')
    .step('Run').run('echo hi').env(MY_SECRET='${{ secrets.MY_SECRET }}')
    .build())
y = yaml_of(doc)
assert 'MY_SECRET' in y['jobs']['test']['steps'][0]['env']

doc = (Workflow('ci').on.push()
    .job('test').runs_on('ubuntu-latest')
    .step('Deploy').run('deploy.sh').if_("github.ref == 'refs/heads/main'")
    .build())
y = yaml_of(doc)
assert 'github.ref' in y['jobs']['test']['steps'][0]['if']

doc = (Workflow('ci').on.push()
    .job('test').runs_on('ubuntu-latest')
    .step('Maybe fail').run('exit 1').continue_on_error(True)
    .build())
y = yaml_of(doc)
assert y['jobs']['test']['steps'][0]['continue-on-error'] is True

doc = (Workflow('ci').on.push()
    .job('test').runs_on('ubuntu-latest')
    .step('Checkout').uses('actions/checkout@v4')
    .step('Setup Python').setup_python('3.12')
    .step('Install').run("pip install -e '.'")
    .step('Test').run('pytest')
    .build())
```

``` python
# environment (GitHub deployment protection)

    .job('deploy-staging').runs_on('ubuntu-latest')
    .environment('staging')
    .step('Deploy').run('./deploy.sh staging')
    .end_job()
    .job('deploy-prod', needs='deploy-staging').runs_on('ubuntu-latest')
    .environment('production')
    .step('Deploy').run('./deploy.sh production')
    .build())

    .job('build').runs_on('ubuntu-latest')

    .step('Build').run('make build')
    .end_job()
    .job('deploy', needs='build').runs_on('ubuntu-latest')
    .step('Deploy').run('echo Deploying ${{ needs.build.outputs.version }}')
    .build())
y = yaml_of(doc)
test_eq(y['jobs']['build']['outputs']['version'], '${{ steps.get_version.outputs.version }}')

# job-level concurrency (only one deploy at a time)

    .job('deploy').runs_on('ubuntu-latest')
    .concurrency('deploy-${{ github.ref }}', cancel_in_progress=False)
    .step('Deploy').run('./deploy.sh')
    .build())
y = yaml_of(doc)
conc = y['jobs']['deploy']['concurrency']
assert 'github.ref' in conc['group']
assert conc['cancel-in-progress'] is False
```

``` python
y = yaml_of(doc)
assert 'lint' not in y['jobs']
assert 'needs' not in y['jobs']['test']

# matrix test
doc = uv_ci(python_versions=['3.11', '3.12', '3.13'])
y = yaml_of(doc)
mat = y['jobs']['test']['strategy']['matrix']
test_eq(len(mat['python-version']), 3)
test_eq(y['jobs']['test']['steps'][1]['with']['python-version'], '${{ matrix.python-version }}')

# include-only matrix survives rendering
wfb_inc = Workflow('ci')
wfb_inc.job('t').runs_on('ubuntu-latest').strategy().include(os='linux').end_strategy().step('a').run('b').end_job()
test_eq(yaml_of(wfb_inc.build())['jobs']['t']['strategy']['matrix']['include'], [{'os': 'linux'}])

# publishing is triggered by releases
assert 'release' in yaml_of(Workflow('p').uv_pypi_job(needs=None).build())['on']

print('uv_ci OK')
```

``` python
# TestRealisticWorkflows
doc = (
    Workflow('openfish-ci')
    .run_name('CI -- ${{ github.actor }} @ ${{ github.sha }}')
    .on
        .push(branches=['main'], paths=['src/**', 'tests/**', 'pyproject.toml'])
        .pull_request(branches=['main'])
    .job('lint')
        .runs_on('ubuntu-latest')
        .timeout_minutes(10)
        .checkout()
        .setup_python('3.12', cache='pip')
        .step('Install dev deps').run("pip install -e '.[dev]'")
        .step('Ruff lint').run('ruff check .')
        .step('Ruff format check').run('ruff format --check .')
        .step('Mypy').run('mypy src/')
        .end_job()
    .job('test', needs='lint')
        .runs_on('${{ matrix.os }}')
        .timeout_minutes(20)
        .env(PYTHONDONTWRITEBYTECODE='1')
        .checkout()
        .step('Setup Python').setup_python('${{ matrix.python-version }}', cache='pip')
        .step('Install').run("pip install -e '.[dev]'")
        .step('Test with coverage').run('pytest --cov=src --cov-report=xml -x')
        .step('Upload coverage').uses('codecov/codecov-action@v4').with_(fail_ci_if_error='false')
        .build()
)
jb = doc._builder._job_map['test']
(
    jb.strategy()
    .matrix(python_version=['3.11', '3.12'], os=['ubuntu-latest', 'macos-latest'])
    .fail_fast(False)
)
y = yaml_of(doc)
test_eq(y['name'], 'openfish-ci')
assert 'lint' in y['jobs']
assert 'test' in y['jobs']
test_eq(y['jobs']['test']['needs'], 'lint')

doc = (
    Workflow('round-trip')
    .on.push(branches=['main']).schedule('0 6 * * 1')

    .step('S2').uses('actions/checkout@v4').with_(fetch_depth=0)
    .build()
)
y = yaml_of(doc)
test_eq(y['on']['schedule'][0]['cron'], '0 6 * * 1')
test_eq(y['jobs']['job1']['steps'][0]['env']['MY_VAR'], 'abc')
test_eq(y['jobs']['job1']['steps'][1]['with']['fetch-depth'], 0)

print('realistic workflows OK')
```

### Full production pipeline

``` python
# TestProductionPipeline
# Full CI/CD: lint → test (matrix+services) → build artifacts → deploy staging → deploy prod
wf = Workflow('production-ci')
wf.run_name('${{ github.actor }}: ${{ github.ref_name }}')
(wf.on
    .push(branches=['main'], tags=['v*'])
    .pull_request(branches=['main'])
    .workflow_dispatch())
wf.concurrency('ci-${{ github.ref }}', cancel_in_progress=True)
wf.permissions(contents='read', packages='write', id_token='write')

# Lint
(wf.job('lint')
    .runs_on('ubuntu-latest')
    .timeout_minutes(10)
    .checkout().end_step()
    .setup_python('3.12').end_step()
    .install("pip install -e '.[dev]'")
    .step('Ruff').run('ruff check . && ruff format --check .')
    .end_job())

# Integration tests with postgres service and matrix strategy
test_job = (wf.job('test', needs='lint')
    .runs_on('ubuntu-latest')
    .timeout_minutes(20)
    .services(postgres={
        'image': 'postgres:15',
        'env': {'POSTGRES_PASSWORD': 'postgres', 'POSTGRES_DB': 'testdb'},
        'ports': ['5432:5432'],
        'options': '--health-cmd pg_isready --health-interval 10s --health-retries 5',
    })
    .env(DATABASE_URL='postgresql://postgres:postgres@localhost/testdb'))
(test_job.strategy()
    .matrix(python_version=['3.11', '3.12'], os=['ubuntu-latest'])
    .exclude(python_version='3.11')
    .fail_fast(False)
    .max_parallel(3)
    .end_strategy()
    .checkout().end_step()
    .step('Cache pip').cache(
        path='~/.cache/pip',
        key="${{ runner.os }}-pip-${{ hashFiles('**/pyproject.toml') }}",
        restore_keys=['${{ runner.os }}-pip-'],
    )
    .step('Setup Python').setup_python('${{ matrix.python-version }}').end_step()
    .install("pip install -e '.[dev]'").end_step()
    .run_tests('pytest -x --cov=src')
    .end_job())

# Build + upload release artifact
(wf.job('build', needs='test')
    .runs_on('ubuntu-latest')
    .if_("startsWith(github.ref, 'refs/tags/v')")
    .outputs(version='${{ steps.get_ver.outputs.version }}')
    .checkout().end_step()
    .setup_python('3.12')
    .step('Get version').run("echo version=${GITHUB_REF#refs/tags/v} >> $GITHUB_OUTPUT").id('get_ver')
    .step('Build wheel').run('pip install build && python -m build')
    .step('Upload dist').upload_artifact('dist', 'dist/', retention_days=30)
    .end_job())

# Deploy to staging (auto, environment protection)
(wf.job('deploy-staging', needs='build')
    .runs_on('ubuntu-latest')
    .environment('staging')
    .concurrency('deploy-staging', cancel_in_progress=True)
    .step('Download dist').download_artifact('dist', 'dist/')
    .step('Deploy staging').run('./scripts/deploy.sh staging ${{ needs.build.outputs.version }}')
    .end_job())

# Deploy to production (manual approval via environment)
(wf.job('deploy-prod', needs='deploy-staging')
    .runs_on('ubuntu-latest')
    .environment('production')
    .concurrency('deploy-prod', cancel_in_progress=False)
    .step('Download dist').download_artifact('dist', 'dist/')
    .step('Deploy prod').run('./scripts/deploy.sh production ${{ needs.build.outputs.version }}')
    .end_job())

y = yaml_of(wf.build())

# Verify full structure
assert list(y['jobs'].keys()) == ['lint', 'test', 'build', 'deploy-staging', 'deploy-prod']
test_eq(y['jobs']['test']['needs'], 'lint')
test_eq(y['jobs']['build']['needs'], 'test')
test_eq(y['jobs']['deploy-staging']['needs'], 'build')
test_eq(y['jobs']['deploy-prod']['needs'], 'deploy-staging')

# Verify matrix + services
mat = y['jobs']['test']['strategy']['matrix']
assert 'python-version' in mat
assert y['jobs']['test']['strategy']['max-parallel'] == 3
assert y['jobs']['test']['strategy']['fail-fast'] is False
assert len(mat['exclude']) == 1
assert 'postgres' in y['jobs']['test']['services']

# Verify environments and concurrency
test_eq(y['jobs']['deploy-staging']['environment'], 'staging')
test_eq(y['jobs']['deploy-prod']['environment'], 'production')
assert y['jobs']['deploy-staging']['concurrency']['cancel-in-progress'] is True
assert y['jobs']['deploy-prod']['concurrency']['cancel-in-progress'] is False

# Verify artifact handoff chain
build_steps = [s['name'] for s in y['jobs']['build']['steps']]
assert 'Upload dist' in build_steps
staging_steps = [s['name'] for s in y['jobs']['deploy-staging']['steps']]
assert 'Download dist' in staging_steps

# Verify job outputs flowing through
test_eq(y['jobs']['build']['outputs']['version'], '${{ steps.get_ver.outputs.version }}')

# Verify triggers
assert 'push' in y['on']
assert 'pull_request' in y['on']
assert 'workflow_dispatch' in y['on']

# Verify workflow-level concurrency
assert y['concurrency']['cancel-in-progress'] is True

print('production pipeline OK')
```

    production pipeline OK

``` python
# TEST_REPO is 'owner/repo' and defaults to vedicreader/sankalpa. A value without '/' disables the integration test.
def _get_test_repo():
    raw = os.environ.get('TEST_REPO', 'vedicreader/sankalpa')
    if '/' not in raw: return None
    owner, repo = raw.split('/', 1)
    return owner, repo
```

``` python
if os.environ.get('GITHUB_TOKEN') and (r:=_get_test_repo()):
    from ghapi.all import GhApi
    token = os.environ['GITHUB_TOKEN']
    owner, repo = r
    workflow_name = 'ghaflow-test-upload'
    doc = (
        Workflow(workflow_name)
        .on.workflow_dispatch()
        .job('hello')
        .runs_on('ubuntu-latest')
        .step('Hello').run("echo 'Hello from ghaflow test!'")
        .build()
    )

    branch = 'ghaflow-test'
    api = GhApi(owner=owner, repo=repo, token=token)

    try: api.repos.get_branch(branch=branch)
    except Exception:
        default = api.repos.get().default_branch
        ref_data = api.git.get_ref(ref=f'heads/{default}')
        sha = ref_data.object.sha
        api.git.create_ref(ref=f'refs/heads/{branch}', sha=sha)

    result = doc.upload(owner=owner,repo=repo,branch=branch,token=token,
        commit_message='test: ghaflow upload integration test')
    assert result is not None

    path = f'.github/workflows/{workflow_name}.yml'
    content = api.repos.get_content(path=path, ref=branch)
    assert content.name == f'{workflow_name}.yml'
    print('integration upload OK')
else: print('Integration tests skipped (GITHUB_TOKEN or TEST_REPO not set)')
```
